## Claude Code

Add Claude-specific notes here only when they are truly host-specific. `CLAUDE.md` is generated by memory-sync from this file plus `@AGENTS.md` — direct edits to `CLAUDE.md` get wiped on the next sync.

### Pipeline skills rely on Claude Code's parallel Agent primitive

Skills under `skills/research/` that summarize long content (`youtube-wiki`, `blog-reader`, `pdf-reader`, `academic-deep-research`, `ml-ablation-design`) dispatch one Agent subagent per chunk in a *single* message. For a 4-hour podcast that's 17 parallel agents fanned out at once. Codex has no equivalent primitive — dogfooding these pipelines from Claude Code is the canonical path. Use `TaskCreate` / `TaskUpdate` to track the multi-step run; the structural-check + artifact-verification loop in AGENTS.md is easy to lose without a task list.

### Before writing a new artifact, read an existing one

The pipeline skills emit faithful digests under `docs/`. Match the shape of what's already there before drafting a new one:

- `docs/videos/2026-05-11-yao-shunyu-*.md` — `youtube-wiki` shape (header metadata, section summaries, verbatim quotes, verification log)
- `docs/wikis/2026-05-11-techshiba-*.md` — `insert-wiki` shape (verbatim body + tags + "Why I saved this")
- `docs/plans/2026-*-design.md` — design-doc shape for new skills
- `docs/github/`, `docs/blogs/`, `docs/research/` — `github-reader` / `blog-reader` / `academic-deep-research`

### Host-specific: `OPENAI_API_KEY` lives in per-project `.env`

On this machine the key is **not** in `~/.zshrc` or `launchctl`; it's in `~/lab/<project>/.env` files (e.g. `~/lab/flask/.env`, `~/lab/web3ai/.env`). When the OpenAI Whisper-API fallback in `youtube-wiki` needs it, source it explicitly — do not assume `echo $OPENAI_API_KEY` works in a fresh shell:

```bash
export OPENAI_API_KEY="$(grep '^OPENAI_API_KEY=' ~/lab/flask/.env | head -1 | cut -d= -f2- | tr -d \"'\\\"\")"
```

### Sub-agent results aren't visible to the user

When a parallel-summarize step finishes, each subagent's report comes back as a tool result in *your* context — not the user's. Have the subagents write their structured notes to disk (e.g. `/tmp/yt-wiki/<slug>.notes.<i>.md`) and return only a short "OK §i" confirmation; then read the files yourself during synthesis. Trying to inline 17 agent responses bloats your context and the user sees none of it anyway.
